newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's says 1997 transition year for US business.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's says 1997 transition year for US business.

text.p: McDonald's Corp. said 1997 is expected to be a year of transition for its U.S. business, with results expected to improve as the year progresses and into 1998.
"We plan to add fewer restaurants than in 1996 and to focus on building sales at existing restaurants," McDonald's executives said in a letter to shareholders contained in the annual report.

"We will emphasize aggressive marketing; a national value initiative; food taste, both in our restaurants and in our advertising; and fast, accurate, friendly service, particularly in the drive-thru where we already have a competitive advantage."
McDonald's added 2,642 restaurants systemwide in 1996, including 1,995 full-size, traditional units and 647 limited menu satellites. This compared with 2,430 restaurants in 1995.

McDonald's, which has more than 21,000 restaurants worldwide and over 12,000 in the United States, has said it plans to add between 2,400 and 2,800 restaurants in 1997. About 70 percent of these new units will be located outside the United States.

In 1996, U.S. systemwide sales rose to $16.37 billion from $15.91 billion, which the company attributed primarily to restaurant expansion. Same-store sales, measuring results from units open at least a year, were negative in 1996, following a rise in 1995. The company blamed an extremely competitive U.S. operating environment and, at times, severe weather and difficult comparisons with the year-ago period.

Outside the United States, McDonald's said it is committed to increasing market share through expansion and comparable sales growth. It hopes to increase profits by lowering average operating and development costs.
Total sales outside the United States in 1996 amounted to $15.44 billion, up from $14 billion.
Overall, the company's systemwide sales were $31.81 billion in 1996, up from $29.91 billion in 1995. Its net income amounted to $1.57 billion, up from $1.43 billion.
McDonald's, in a glossy annual report that resembles a magazine, said it continues to use its global buying power to cut costs.

It added that global purchasing and other initiatives resulted in nearly $300 million in annualized savings in 1996, bringing the cumulative identified systemwide savings to about $900 million over the past five years.
